# Plan: Iterative/Cyclical Workflow Navigation

## TL;DR

The reported bug is that back-navigation tab/step clicks call `switchTab()` only — they never call `backToPhase()` — so the backend phase stays at the later stage while the UI shows an earlier tab. The user is visually on "Job Input" but the backend is in `customization`, with no clean forward path. Beyond the bug fix, the full iterative-workflow vision requires: a two-mode back-nav modal (view vs. rerun), backend stale-phase tracking, frontend dirty visualization across all step pills, and document updates.

---

## Root Cause of Reported Bug

- `handleStepClick()` ([web/workflow-steps.js:630](web/workflow-steps.js)) and the tab-click guard ([web/ui-core.js:488](web/ui-core.js)) both call only `switchTab(tabName)` on confirm
- `backToPhase()` ([web/workflow-steps.js:95]) — which POSTs to `/api/back-to-phase` and repositions the backend phase — is never called from these navigation paths
- Result: backend remains at `customization` while the UI shows Job Input. Forward navigation from that "stranded" state is undefined

---

## Phases of Work

### Phase 0: Document existing gaps first (before any code)

Update documents to capture the full design intent, so implementation has clear acceptance criteria.

**Steps:**
0a. Update `tasks/gaps.md`:
   - Update GAP-02 (Iterative Refinement / Phase Re-Entry) — mark root cause, add missing wiring, tweak acceptance criteria
   - Update GAP-14 (Workflow Orientation) — add "view vs. rerun" back-nav modal requirement
   - Update GAP-18 (Workflow Stage Re-Run Completeness) — add detail on two-mode modal, dirty state propagation, changed-item highlighting
   - Add new GAP-25: "Back-navigation does not call backToPhase() — backend phase not repositioned on tab/step click"

0b. Update `tasks/current-implemented-workflow.md`:
   - Add subsection: "Back Navigation Modes" (view-only vs. rerun)
   - Add subsection: "Downstream Dirty State" model (which fields are invalidated by a rerun of each step)
   - Add subsection: "Iterative Cycle" — describe the expected loop (rerun step N → stale pills on N+1...end → user re-executes each stale step forward)

0c. Update user story files:
   - `tasks/user-story-applicant.md`: Add US-A12 detail (currently mentioned but incomplete) — acceptance criteria for back-navigation view mode, rerun mode, and dirty-state visualization
   - `tasks/user-story-ux-expert.md`: Update US-U1 or add US-U10 for two-mode modal UX, stale step visuals, and forward progress from any restarted step
   - `tasks/user-story-power-user.md`: Add story for ad-hoc iteration (rerun any step at any time without starting a new session)

0d. Update `ARCHITECTURE.md`: Add state-machine diagram section showing backward arcs and the `dirty_phases` orthogonal state.

---

### Phase 1: Fix the Back-Navigation Bug (bug fix)

**Goal:** Clicking a completed step pill or completed second-level tab actually repositions the backend phase.

**Steps:**
1a. **Two-mode confirm modal** — replace the single "Proceed" button in the confirm modal with two choices:
   - "View (read-only)" — repositions backend via `backToPhase(step)` then `switchTab(tab)`; does NOT re-run LLM
   - "Rerun this step" — calls `reRunPhase(step)` which re-executes LLM and then navigates
   - Files: `web/workflow-steps.js` (_showReRunConfirmModal function), `web/index.html` (modal template)

1b. **Wire `backToPhase()` into step-click handler** — in `handleStepClick()` ([web/workflow-steps.js:630]), when user confirms "View (read-only)", call `await backToPhase(step, '')` before `switchTab()`.

1c. **Wire `backToPhase()` into tab-click guard** — in the tab `addEventListener('click', ...)` at [web/ui-core.js:488], same fix.

1d. **Fix forward navigation from a backed-into phase** — after `backToPhase()`, the step pill for that step should become `active` (not `completed`) so the user can advance forward again. This is already handled by `updateWorkflowSteps()` reading from `/api/status` — verify it works after the fix.

---

### Phase 2: Backend Stale-Phase Tracking

**Goal:** When a step is rerun, the backend knows which downstream steps are now stale. This is the foundation for dirty visualization and future phase-gating.

**Steps:**
2a. Add `PHASE_PRODUCES` registry in `scripts/utils/conversation_manager.py`:
   - Maps each Phase to the state keys it populates
   - Example: `Phase.JOB_ANALYSIS → ['job_analysis', 'post_analysis_questions']`
   - Example: `Phase.CUSTOMIZATION → ['customizations', 'experience_decisions', 'skill_decisions', ...]`

2b. Add `stale_phases: set` to session state — default `set()`. Updated in `re_run_phase()` and `back_to_phase()`.

2c. Update `re_run_phase()` in `conversation_manager.py` (~line 1145):
   - Compute all phases downstream of the target
   - Add them to `state['stale_phases']`
   - Optionally move (not delete) downstream state keys to `state['prior_<key>']` so they're available for diff display but not active

2d. Update `back_to_phase()` in `conversation_manager.py` (~line 1118):
   - Add all phases forward of the target to `state['stale_phases']`
   - (This is "view mode" — no clearing, just marking stale)

2e. Clear a phase from `stale_phases` when that phase completes successfully (in the forward-path phase-advance code at each transition point).

2f. Expose `stale_phases` (as a list) in the `GET /api/status` response (StatusResponse schema in `scripts/routes/`) so the frontend can read it.

---

### Phase 3: Frontend Dirty Visualization

**Goal:** Step pills and second-level tabs show stale state visually when downstream of a rerun.

**Steps:**
3a. Add `stale` CSS class to step pills in `web/styles.css`:
   - Visual: warning-colored pill (amber/orange border, slightly faded label)
   - Does not conflict with existing `active`, `completed`, `locked` classes

3b. Update `updateWorkflowSteps(status)` in `web/workflow-steps.js` (~line 520):
   - Read `status.stale_phases` from the status response
   - Apply `stale` class to corresponding `step-<name>` elements
   - Stale steps should remain clickable (can navigate to view or rerun them)

3c. Update second-level tab staleness:
   - Tabs belonging to a stale stage get a visual badge (similar to existing `tab-stale` for layout) 
   - Extend the existing `tab-stale` class usage to all stages, not just layout

3d. Add "Stale" tooltip text to stale step pills:
   - "This step may be outdated — a previous step was re-run. Click to view or rerun."

---

### Phase 4: "View Mode" UX Polish (depends on Phase 1 + Phase 3)

**Goal:** Make the "view earlier info" case smooth — user can browse old analysis/decisions without triggering re-runs.

**Steps:**
4a. When a step is in "view mode" (backed into, not rerun), show a read-only banner at the top of each second-level tab:
   - "Viewing [step name] (read-only). To update this step, click Rerun."

4b. Add a "Rerun This Step" button/link in the read-only banner — calls `reRunPhase(step)`.

4c. From a view-mode step, "Continue Forward" button (or Next pill click) should advance to the next step without re-running:
   - Click next step pill → since current step is "view mode" not "stale", just navigate without modal

---

### Phase 5: Changed-Item Highlighting on Rerun (deferred, tracked in GAP-18)

**Goal:** After a rerun, show diff between prior and new LLM output inline.

- Backend: `prior_<key>` fields are already populated by `re_run_phase()`
- Frontend: Display old vs. new values side-by-side or with strike-through in Analysis, Customizations tabs
- This is already tracked as open in GAP-18; call out as deferred from this workstream

---

## Relevant Files

- `web/workflow-steps.js` — `handleStepClick()`, `backToPhase()`, `reRunPhase()`, `_showReRunConfirmModal()`, `updateWorkflowSteps()`
- `web/ui-core.js` — tab click guard, `updateTabBarForStage()`, `switchTab()`
- `web/index.html` — confirm modal template, step pill markup
- `web/state-manager.js` — `PHASE_TO_STEP`, `PHASES`, stale state fields
- `web/styles.css` — stale pill CSS class
- `scripts/utils/conversation_manager.py` — `back_to_phase()`, `re_run_phase()`, Phase enum, `PHASE_PRODUCES` registry (new)
- `scripts/routes/job_routes.py` — `POST /api/back-to-phase`, `POST /api/re-run-phase`
- `scripts/routes/` — StatusResponse schema (add `stale_phases`)
- `tasks/gaps.md` — GAP-02, GAP-14, GAP-18, new GAP-25
- `tasks/current-implemented-workflow.md` — back nav modes, dirty state model, iterative cycle description
- `tasks/user-story-applicant.md` — US-A12 acceptance criteria expansion
- `tasks/user-story-ux-expert.md` — US-U1 update / US-U10 new
- `tasks/user-story-power-user.md` — new story
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — state machine backward arcs, stale_phases orthogonal state

## Verification

1. Navigate to a session in `customization` phase → click "Job Input" step pill → confirm "View" → verify GET `/api/status` shows `phase == 'init'` or `phase == 'job_analysis'` (backed-into phase)
2. From that backed-into "Job Input" view, click "Analysis" step pill → verify navigation to Analysis tab works
3. From "Analysis" tab (backed-into), click "Rerun This Step" → verify LLM re-executes and `stale_phases` includes `customization`, `rewrite_review`, etc.
4. Verify downstream step pills show stale visual on the step bar
5. Click a stale downstream pill → verify confirm modal offers "View" and "Rerun" options
6. Complete a stale step → verify that step's stale marker clears
7. Run Python tests: `conda run -n cvgen python -m pytest tests/test_conversation_manager.py -q --tb=short`
8. Run JS tests: `npm run test:js`

## Decisions / Scope

- Phase 0 (docs) is prerequisite to Phase 1 (code), to ensure acceptance criteria are clear
- Phase 5 (changed-item highlighting) is deferred — tracked in GAP-18
- The `PHASE_PRODUCES` registry in Phase 2 is additive only — no existing phase-transition guards are changed
- The harvest write-back guard (`_require_harvest_apply_phase`) is NOT changed by this work
- Master CV write protection rules remain unchanged
- No changes to the CLI path (`llm_cv_generator.py`)

## Further Considerations

1. **"View mode" should NOT call `/api/back-to-phase`** if the backend is already at a later phase — the user may just want to peek at earlier data. But currently there's no way to "view without repositioning". This needs a decision: should we add a `view_only=true` param to `/api/back-to-phase`? Or should the frontend keep a "local view tab" concept without touching the backend?
2. **Stale vs. invalid distinction**: Stale means "this step ran but may be outdated"; invalid means "this step has never run from the current inputs". The current model only has `completed` and `not completed`. Adding `stale` as a third state has implications for the step pill visual design — confirm the three-state design is acceptable before implementation.
3. **Session restore**: After browser refresh, if the session was in view-mode (backed into an earlier phase), should the app restore to the viewed tab or to the phase pointer? Currently it restores to the phase pointer. This should be decided and documented.

# Plan: Navigation Browse/Rerun State Model

## TL;DR

The step bar currently conflates two distinct concepts into one visual state: **where the backend workflow IS** (application phase) vs. **what the user is currently LOOKING AT** (view cursor). This causes the bug where browsing back to "Job Input" looks like abandoning progress, and the path home is invisible. The fix introduces a two-signal step pill model and wires back-navigation to distinguish "browse" from "rerun".

---

## Research Findings

### Root Cause
- `updateWorkflowSteps(status)` assigns `.step.active` (blue) to the backend phase step; `.step.completed.clickable` to prior steps.
- `switchTab(tabName)` updates `stateManager.currentTab` but does NOT update step pill classes.
- Result: when browsing to an earlier tab, no step pill changes — the user has no visual anchor for where they came from or where their work is.
- The `active` pill is NOT marked `.clickable` — so the user may not even know they can click it to return. 
- `getVisibleStage()` resolves via `currentTab` first, so the view cursor IS tracked in state — just never displayed.

### What Exists (infrastructure)
- `backToPhase(step)` → `POST /api/back-to-phase` — repositions backend phase without clearing downstream (wired to wrong trigger)
- `reRunPhase(step)` → `POST /api/re-run-phase` — re-runs LLM call, stores `prior_X` for diff display (also wrong trigger)
- `_showReRunConfirmModal(step, 'back-nav', callback)` — modal exists but callback is only `switchTab()`, never `backToPhase()`
- `.step.stale` and `.step.stale-critical` CSS already defined (amber/red) — not used on step pills
- `isLayoutStale` spec in `tasks/layout-stale-ui-spec.md` covers only layout step
- GAP-02, GAP-14, GAP-18 all identify this as incomplete

### Two-Concept Confusion
| Concept | Current signal | Problem |
|---------|---------------|---------|
| Backend phase (app state) | `.step.active` (blue) | Doesn't move when user browses |
| Viewing cursor | Nothing visible | Completely invisible |

## Steps

### Phase A — CSS/Visual: Separate App-State from View Cursor

**Goal**: Two independent visual signals on step pills.

1. **Add `.step.viewing` CSS rule** in `web/styles.css` — a "you are looking at this" ring:
   - `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #3b82f6` (blue ring, distinct from the pill fill)
   - Or: a small triangle/chevron below the pill (`:after` pseudo-element)
   - Must be visible even on `completed` (green) and `active` (blue) pills
   - Must stack cleanly with `.stale` modifier

2. **Rename/clarify `.step.active`** to mean exclusively "backend app phase is here":
   - Keep `active` class name for backward compat (used everywhere)
   - Add `.step.active` cursor: pointer — currently missing, making "click to return" invisible
   - Consider distinct green hue for `active` (≥ completed brightness) to signal "this is home, work continues here"

3. **New `.step.browsing-away` state on the `active` pill** when `viewing ≠ active`:
   - Subtle pulsing or thicker/different border: shows "your work is here, you're currently browsing elsewhere"
   - Optionally: tooltip/title="Return to active step"

**Files**: `web/styles.css`

---

### Phase B — JS: Emit Viewing Indicator on Tab/Step Switch

**Goal**: The viewing cursor updates every time any tab or step is clicked.

4. **New helper `_updateViewingIndicator(tabName)`** in `web/workflow-steps.js` (or `web/ui-core.js`):
   - Removes `.viewing` from all `.step` elements
   - Adds `.viewing` to `#step-{stage}` where `stage = getStageForTab(tabName)`
   - Also toggles `.browsing-away` on the `app-active` step if `stage !== activeStep`

5. **Call `_updateViewingIndicator(tab)`** from `switchTab()` (after `stateManager.setCurrentTab(tab)`)
   - `switchTab` is in `web/review-table-base.js` — add call there
   - Also call from `handleStepClick` after any navigation

6. **Call `_updateViewingIndicator(currentTab)`** from `updateWorkflowSteps(status)` at end (to re-sync on every status fetch)

**Files**: `web/workflow-steps.js`, `web/review-table-base.js` (or `web/ui-core.js`)

---

### Phase C — Fix Back-Navigation: "Browse" vs "Rerun" Modal

**Goal**: The confirmation modal clearly distinguishes browsing (view only) from re-running (phase change + LLM).

7. **Update `_showReRunConfirmModal()`** in `web/workflow-steps.js` to support two distinct callback slots:
   - `onBrowse` callback → just `switchTab(tabName)` (no phase change)
   - `onRerun` callback → `reRunPhase(step, feedback)` (phase change + LLM)

8. **Update all call-sites** of `_showReRunConfirmModal` in both `handleStepClick` (workflow-steps.js) and the tab-click guard (ui-core.js `setupEventListeners`):
   - Pass `onBrowse: () => switchTab(tabName)` 
   - Pass `onRerun: () => reRunPhase(step)` 

9. **Modal text changes**:
   - Title: "View or re-run [Step Name]?"
   - Body: "You have completed downstream steps. Choose whether you just want to review, or want to re-run this step and update downstream results."
   - Button 1: "Browse only" (outline) → `onBrowse`
   - Button 2: "Re-run step" (solid primary) → `onRerun`
   - Button 3: "Cancel" → dismiss

10. **Make `.step.active` have explicit `cursor: pointer` and `clickable` behavior** — add `.clickable` class to `active` steps in `updateWorkflowSteps` (or add pointer to active CSS rule and wire click handler)

**Files**: `web/workflow-steps.js`, `web/ui-core.js`

### Phase D — Backend: Phase-Level Stale State

**Goal**: When a step is re-run, downstream steps become visually stale (amber), not just layout.

11. **Add `stale_steps` set to `ConversationManager` session state** in `scripts/utils/conversation_manager.py`:
    - Populated by `re_run_phase(target)`: mark all steps after `target` in `_STEP_ORDER` as stale
    - Cleared step-by-step as each step is re-executed
    - Exposed via `GET /api/status` response

12. **`PHASE_PRODUCES` mapping** (what state keys each phase produces) in `conversation_manager.py`:
    - Maps each phase to its output state keys (for future invalidation if needed)
    - Used by `re_run_phase` to identify which `prior_X` fields to archive before overwrite

13. **Expose `stale_steps` in `StatusResponse`** (scripts/utils/schemas or web_app.py):
    - Frontend reads `status.stale_steps: string[]`

14. **`updateWorkflowSteps(status)`** reads `status.stale_steps`:
    - For each step in `stale_steps`: add `.stale` modifier class (amber, already defined in CSS)
    - `.stale` stacks on top of `.completed` or `.active`

**Files**: `scripts/utils/conversation_manager.py`, relevant route files for status, `web/workflow-steps.js`

## Verification

1. **Browse test**: At Customization phase, click Job Input → confirm Browse → job tab shows; step bar shows Customization pill with browsing-away pulse; Job Input pill shows viewing ring. Click Customization pill → returns immediately, viewing ring moves back. No backend state changed.
2. **Rerun test**: Same setup → confirm Rerun Job Input → `POST /api/re-run-phase` fires → `status.stale_steps` contains `analysis`, `customizations`, `rewrite`, `spell`, `generate`, `layout`, `finalise` → all those pills show amber stale modifier → user sees visually which steps need re-running.
3. **Viewing coincidence test**: At Customization phase viewing customization tab → only app-active class active, no `.viewing` class visible on pill (or they overlap cleanly).
4. **Session restore**: Reload with session at Customization, currentTab=job → step bar shows Customization as app-active, job tab viewing ring. Correct on first render without user interaction.
5. **Run JS test suite**: `npm run test:js` — all 104 tests pass.
6. **Run Python test suite**: `conda run -n cvgen python run_tests.py --categories unit component` — all pass.

---

## Decisions

- **Browse vs. rerun are separate intents** — combining them in the modal was the architectural error; splitting them is the fix.
- **`active` step must be `clickable`** — currently the "return home" affordance is invisible; fix is cursor+click wiring.
- **Phase-level staleness** extends (does not replace) the existing layout staleness spec — two orthogonal signals.
- **Excluded**: auto-clearing downstream state on rerun (preserve-all remains the policy per copilot-instructions.md); auto-navigating user to active step on browse completion.
- **Deferred**: changed-item highlighting (GAP-02, GAP-18) — still a gap but not part of this plan.

---

## Further Considerations

1. **Visual encoding for overlapping states**: when a step is both `active` (app home) AND `viewing` (user is there), consider showing only the `active` marker (don't double-ring). Implies the `.viewing` class is suppressed on the `active` step.
2. **"Browsing" banner vs. step pill indicator**: the browsing-away contextual signal could live in the step bar (pulse on active pill) OR as a thin banner below the step bar ("Browsing Job Input — your workflow is at Customise"). The banner approach is more discoverable. Both are additive.
3. **`backToPhase` vs `reRunPhase` for Rerun button**: the modal's "Re-run step" could reasonably call `backToPhase` (reposition only, no immediate LLM call) and then the user presses the normal action button for that step. Alternatively, `reRunPhase` immediately re-runs the LLM. Former is less surprising; latter is more intent-aligned. Recommend `backToPhase` + let user click action button (safer, mirrors existing UX pattern).

```
### Phase A — CSS/Visual: Separate App-State from View Cursor

**Goal**: Two independent visual signals on step pills — fill encodes app state (where work is), ring encodes view cursor (what's on screen).

#### Four-State Visual Matrix

Every pill is in exactly ONE of four states, determined by two binary conditions:
- **Is this the app-active step?** (backend `phase` maps to this step)
- **Is this the currently viewed step?** (`stateManager.currentTab` maps to this step)

| App state = this step? | Viewing = this step? | Pill state | CSS classes | Visual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | **At home** | `.step.active` | Blue fill (`#dbeafe`/`#1d4ed8`), no ring — fill IS the signal, ring suppressed to avoid noise |
| ✅ Yes | ❌ No | **Home, browsing away** | `.step.active.browsing-away` | Blue fill + pulsing amber-gold outer ring (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #f59e0b`) + title="Return to active step" |
| ❌ No (completed) | ✅ Yes | **Reviewing a past step** | `.step.completed.viewing` | Green fill (`#dcfce7`/`#166534`) + solid blue ring (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #3b82f6`) |
| ❌ No (completed) | ❌ No | **Done, not in view** | `.step.completed` | Green fill only — no change from today |

**Upcoming steps** (neither active nor completed): gray fill, no ring, not clickable — unchanged.

**Stale modifier (.stale)**: amber tint stacks on top of either `completed` or `active` fill; ring still visible on top. Stale-critical: red tint.

#### Ring Design Rationale

- **Blue ring** (`#3b82f6`) = "your eye is here" — echoes the tab-bar active blue, deliberately links viewing cursor to the second-level tabs already colored blue.
- **Amber outer ring** (`#f59e0b`) on `.browsing-away` = "come back" signal — warm urgency without being alarming; matches the existing `.step.stale` amber vocabulary.
- **No ring on `.step.active` when also viewing** — suppressing the ring here avoids visual conflict between fill and ring of the same blue family. The filled pill is sufficient.

#### Browsing-Away Animation

`.step.browsing-away` ring pulses: `animation: browsing-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite` — alternates between `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #f59e0b` and `box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(245,158,11,0.3)`. One gentle, slow pulse cycle. No bounce, no flash.

#### Hover State for Rerun Button

On `.step.completed:hover`, the `↻` span transitions from `opacity: 0` to `opacity: 1` (already implemented). The ring (if present) stays; the `↻` appears inside the pill at pill-right.

#### CSS Changes

1. Add `.step.viewing` — `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #3b82f6; transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease`
2. Add `.step.browsing-away` — `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #f59e0b; animation: browsing-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite`
3. Add `@keyframes browsing-pulse` 
4. Add `cursor: pointer` to `.step.active` (currently missing — blocks "click to return")
5. Add `title` attribute logic in JS: `.step.active` when browsing-away gets `title="Return to active step"`
6. **Suppress `.viewing` on `.step.active`** — in `_updateViewingIndicator`, skip adding `.viewing` to the pill that already has `.active`

**Files**: `web/styles.css`
```

### Phase A — CSS/Visual: Separate App-State from View Cursor

**Goal**: Two independent visual signals on step pills — fill encodes app state (where work is), ring encodes view cursor (what's on screen). The ring is unconditional: it always appears on whichever step is currently visible, regardless of app state.

#### Four-State Visual Matrix

Every pill is in exactly ONE of four states, determined by two binary conditions:
- **Is this the app-active step?** (backend `phase` maps to this step)
- **Is this the currently viewed step?** (`stateManager.currentTab` maps to this step)

| App state = this step? | Viewing = this step? | Pill state | CSS classes | Visual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | **At home** | `.step.active.viewing` | Blue fill + solid blue ring |
| ✅ Yes | ❌ No | **Home, browsing away** | `.step.active.browsing-away` | Blue fill + pulsing amber ring |
| ❌ No (completed) | ✅ Yes | **Reviewing a past step** | `.step.completed.viewing` | Green fill + solid blue ring |
| ❌ No (completed) | ❌ No | **Done, not in view** | `.step.completed` | Green fill, no ring |

**Upcoming steps** (neither active nor completed): gray fill, no ring, not clickable — unchanged.

**Stale modifier (.stale)**: amber fill tint stacks on top of either `completed` or `active` fill; ring still renders on top. Stale-critical: red tint.

#### Ring Design

- **Blue ring** (`#3b82f6`, `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #3b82f6`) = "your eye is here" — unconditionally applied to the viewed step. Echoes the tab-bar active blue, deliberately linking the view cursor to the second-level tabs.
- **Blue ring on `.step.active` when also viewing**: the ring is visually distinguishable from the blue fill because fill is a light blue (`#dbeafe`) while the ring is the saturated brand blue (`#3b82f6`). They read as "fill = state, ring = position" even in the same color family.
- **Amber pulsing ring** (`#f59e0b`) on `.browsing-away`: replaces the blue ring on the active pill when the user is elsewhere. Warm urgency — "your work is waiting here, come back."

#### Animation

`.step.browsing-away` ring pulses: `animation: browsing-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite` — alternates between `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #f59e0b` and `box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(245,158,11,0.3)`. Slow, gentle. No bounce, no flash.

`.step.viewing` ring: `transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease` only — steady, no pulse. Browsing is calm.

#### Ring Mutual Exclusivity on the Active Pill

- When `active` pill IS the viewed step → `.active.viewing` → blue ring
- When `active` pill is NOT the viewed step → `.active.browsing-away` → amber ring
- **Only one ring at a time on the active pill.** `_updateViewingIndicator` adds `.viewing` to the viewed pill; `updateWorkflowSteps` adds `.browsing-away` to the active pill when they differ. The CSS rule order ensures only the applicable ring color appears.

#### Hover State for Rerun Button

On `.step.completed:hover`, the `↻` span transitions from `opacity: 0` to `opacity: 1` (already implemented). The ring (if present) stays; `↻` appears inside the pill at pill-right. No rerun button on `.step.active` (user presses the step's own action button instead).

#### CSS Changes

1. Add `.step.viewing` — `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #3b82f6; transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease`
2. Add `.step.browsing-away` — `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #f59e0b; animation: browsing-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite`
3. Add `@keyframes browsing-pulse`
4. Add `cursor: pointer` to `.step.active` (currently missing — blocks "click to return")
5. Add `title` attribute logic in JS: `.step.active.browsing-away` gets `title="Return to active step"`
6. **No suppression of `.viewing` on the active pill** — the blue ring appears there too; the light fill vs. saturated ring distinguishes fill from cursor signal

**Files**: `web/styles.css`
```

### Phase A — CSS/Visual: Separate App-State from View Cursor

**Goal**: Two independent visual signals on step pills — fill encodes app state (where work is), ring encodes view cursor (what's on screen).

#### Four-State Visual Matrix

Every pill is in exactly ONE of four states, determined by two binary conditions:
- **Is this the app-active step?** (backend `phase` maps to this step)
- **Is this the currently viewed step?** (`stateManager.currentTab` maps to this step)

| App state = this step? | Viewing = this step? | Pill state | CSS classes | Visual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | **At home** | `.step.active` | Blue fill (`#dbeafe`/`#1d4ed8`), no ring — fill IS the signal, ring suppressed to avoid noise |
| ✅ Yes | ❌ No | **Home, browsing away** | `.step.active.browsing-away` | Blue fill + pulsing amber-gold outer ring (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #f59e0b`) + title="Return to active step" |
| ❌ No (completed) | ✅ Yes | **Reviewing a past step** | `.step.completed.viewing` | Green fill (`#dcfce7`/`#166534`) + solid blue ring (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #3b82f6`) |
| ❌ No (completed) | ❌ No | **Done, not in view** | `.step.completed` | Green fill only — no change from today |

**Upcoming steps** (neither active nor completed): gray fill, no ring, not clickable — unchanged.

**Stale modifier (.stale)**: amber tint stacks on top of either `completed` or `active` fill; ring still visible on top. Stale-critical: red tint.

#### Ring Design Rationale

- **Blue ring** (`#3b82f6`) = "your eye is here" — echoes the tab-bar active blue, deliberately links viewing cursor to the second-level tabs already colored blue.
- **Amber outer ring** (`#f59e0b`) on `.browsing-away` = "come back" signal — warm urgency without being alarming; matches the existing `.step.stale` amber vocabulary.
- **No ring on `.step.active` when also viewing** — suppressing the ring here avoids visual conflict between fill and ring of the same blue family. The filled pill is sufficient.

#### Browsing-Away Animation

`.step.browsing-away` ring pulses: `animation: browsing-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite` — alternates between `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #f59e0b` and `box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(245,158,11,0.3)`. One gentle, slow pulse cycle. No bounce, no flash.

#### Hover State for Rerun Button

On `.step.completed:hover`, the `↻` span transitions from `opacity: 0` to `opacity: 1` (already implemented). The ring (if present) stays; the `↻` appears inside the pill at pill-right.

#### CSS Changes

1. Add `.step.viewing` — `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #3b82f6; transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease`
2. Add `.step.browsing-away` — `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #f59e0b; animation: browsing-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite`
3. Add `@keyframes browsing-pulse` 
4. Add `cursor: pointer` to `.step.active` (currently missing — blocks "click to return")
5. Add `title` attribute logic in JS: `.step.active` when browsing-away gets `title="Return to active step"`
6. **Suppress `.viewing` on `.step.active`** — in `_updateViewingIndicator`, skip adding `.viewing` to the pill that already has `.active`

#### CSS Changes

#### Tooltips

Bootstrap 5 tooltips (already available) are used so tooltips can be styled and positioned consistently with the rest of the UI. The `data-bs-toggle="tooltip"` attribute is set on each step pill element, and `data-bs-title` is updated dynamically in `updateWorkflowSteps` / `_updateViewingIndicator` whenever state changes.

A single `bootstrap.Tooltip` instance is created per pill on first render and updated by calling `tip.setContent({'.tooltip-inner': newText})` on each re-render (Bootstrap 5 API).

**Tooltip text per state:**

| State | Condition | Tooltip text |
|---|---|---|
| At home | `active + viewing` | "**Active step** — your workflow is here and you are viewing it. The ↻ button reruns this step." |
| Home, browsing away | `active + not viewing` (amber ring) | "**Active step** — your workflow is paused here. Click to return." |
| Reviewing a past step | `completed + viewing` | "**Completed** — you are reviewing this step. Hover over the pill to see the rerun option." |
| Done, not in view | `completed + not viewing` | "**Completed** — click to review. Hover to see the rerun option." |
| Stale (any) | `stale` modifier added | Appends: " Results may need updating after upstream changes." |
| Stale-critical | `stale-critical` modifier | Appends: " Output files are outdated — regeneration required." |
| Upcoming | neither active nor completed | "**Not yet reached** — complete earlier steps to unlock [Step Name]." |

Tooltip placement: `data-bs-placement="bottom"` on all pills. Delay: `show: 400, hide: 100` — fast enough to be responsive, slow enough not to fire on pass-through mouse movement.

**Files**: `web/workflow-steps.js`, `web/styles.css` (tooltip init, no custom CSS needed beyond Bootstrap defaults)
```
